nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُ هَوَاهُ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: He does not desire anything without following it.
Someone else said: One of them would worship a stone, and when he saw a stone better than it, he would take it and abandon the first.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-Ḥasan's statement on this is a comprehensive one, i.e. he follows his desire and gives it preference, so it has become for him in the position of a god.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿أَفَأَنتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَكِيلاً﴾.
It was said: a guardian.
And it was said: a surety.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿أَمْ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ أَوْ يَعْقِلُونَ إِنْ هُمْ إِلاَّ كَٱلأَنْعَامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلاًً﴾.
Because the cattle glorify (Allah), and avoid what harms them.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ﴾.
"تَرَى" here stands in the place of "تَعْلَم" (you know).
It may also be from seeing with the eye.
Al-Ḥasan, Abū Mālik, Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said about His saying, the Exalted, ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ﴾: It is what lies between the break of dawn and the rising of the sun.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُ سَاكِناً﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: i.e. had He willed, He would have left it as shade just as it is.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: i.e. had He willed, He would have made the whole day shade.
Qatāda said: ﴿سَاكِنَاً﴾ means permanent.
﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا ٱلشَّمْسَ عَلَيْهِ دَلِيلاً﴾ i.e. it follows it and pursues it.
﴿ثُمَّ قَبَضْنَاهُ إلَيْنَا قَبْضَاً يَسِيرَاً﴾: Sufyān narrated from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rufayʿ, from Mujāhid: ﴿يَسِيرَاً﴾ i.e. hidden (imperceptible).
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: quickly.
Abū Mālik and Ibrāhīm al-Taymī said: ﴿قَبْضَاً يَسِيَراً﴾ is what the sun withdraws of the shade.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Mujāhid's statement is more fitting in Arabic and closer to the meaning, for what we shall mention.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, described His subtlety and His power, and said: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ﴾, i.e. what lies between the break of dawn and the rising of the sun, as the people of tafsīr said, and as I explained to you regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic, in His description of Paradise: ﴿وَظِلٍّ مَمْدُوْدٍ﴾.
Then He, Glorified is He, said ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُ سَاكِناً﴾.
i.e. permanent, as in Paradise. ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا ٱلشَّمْسَ عَلَيْهِ دَلِيلاً﴾ i.e. it points to it and to its meaning, because a thing points to its opposite: light points to darkness, and heat to cold.
And it was said: (it is) pointing to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
﴿ثُمَّ قَبَضْنَاهُ إلَيْنَا قَبْضاًَ يَسِيرَاً﴾ i.e. when the sun sets, the shade is withdrawn in a hidden (gradual) withdrawal: whenever a part of it is withdrawn, a part of darkness is put in its place, and it does not disappear all at once. This is Mujāhid's statement.
The statement of Abū Mālik and Ibrāhīm al-Taymī is that the meaning is: then We withdrew the shade by the coming of the sun.
And they both hold that the meaning of ﴿يَسِيراً﴾ is easy for Us.
Mujāhid's statement is more fitting, because "ثُمَّ" (then) indicates that the second comes after the first; and his statement is also more comprehensive of the meaning.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱللَّيْلَ لِبَاساً﴾.
i.e. a covering. ﴿وَٱلنَّوْمَ سُبَاتاً﴾ i.e. rest. ﴿وَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ نُشُوراً﴾ i.e. one disperses (goes out about one's affairs) in it.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَرْسَلَ ٱلرِّيَاحَ بُشْرَى بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾.
Most of the readers read what has the sense of mercy as "الرياح" (winds, plural), and what has the sense of punishment as "الرِّيح" (wind, singular).
Some of them adduce as evidence a weak ḥadīth narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, that when the wind blew he would say: "O Allah, make it winds (رياحاً), and do not make it a wind (ريحاً)."
Abū Jaʿfar said: It was also said: this came about this way only because the winds that bring mercy are three: al-ṣabā (the east wind), al-shamāl (the north wind) and al-janūb (the south wind).
The fourth is "al-dabūr" (the west wind), and it hardly ever brings rain.
So for what brings mercy it was said: "winds" (رياح).
That said, the ḥadīth has no basis.
The meaning of ﴿نُشْرَاً﴾ is: revival, i.e. they bring the clouds in which there is rain, by which is the life of creation; and ﴿نُشُرَاً﴾ is the plural of نَشُوْر.
It is narrated from ʿĀṣim: ﴿بُشُرَاً﴾, the plural of بَشِيرة (bearer of good tidings).
And it is narrated from him: ﴿بُشْرَاً﴾, with the ḍamma dropped because of its heaviness, or it may be the plural of بُشْرة, as one says: بُسْرةٌ and بُسْرٌ.
And from Muḥammad al-Yamānī: ﴿بُشْرَى﴾, i.e. good tidings.
﴿بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ i.e. the rain.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً طَهُوراًً. لِّنُحْيِـيَ بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتاً وَنُسْقِيَهِ مِمَّا خَلَقْنَآ أَنْعَاماً وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيراً﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd (al-Mubarrad) said: ﴿أَنَاسِيَّ﴾ is the plural of إنْسِيٌّ, like "كُرْسِيٌّ" and كَرَاسِيُّ.
Someone else said: ﴿أَنَاسِيَّ﴾ is the plural of إنسان, the original being "أناسين", like سَرَاحين; then a yāʾ was substituted for the nūn.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
Then He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَاهُ بَيْنَهُمْ لِيَذَّكَّرُواْ﴾.
Meaning the rain, i.e. We water one land and leave another.
﴿لِيَذَّكَّرُواْ﴾ i.e. so that they reflect on the blessings of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and praise Him.
﴿فَأَبَىٰ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ إِلاَّ كُفُوراً﴾: that is their saying: "We were given rain by such-and-such a nawʾ", i.e. by the setting of such-and-such a star, as the astrologers say.
So He made them disbelievers by that.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَاهِدْهُمْ بِهِ جِهَاداً كَبيراً﴾.
i.e. with the Qurʾān.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ﴾.
i.e. He mixed them and let them loose, so they appear mixed to the eye, while between them is a barrier from the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
In the ḥadīth: (مَرِجَتْ أماناتُهمْ) "their trusts became confused", i.e. mixed up.
And one says: مَرَجَ السُّلطانُ النَّاسَ, i.e. the ruler let the people loose; and أمرجتُ الدابَّةَ and مرجتُها: i.e. I let the animal loose to graze.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿هَـٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ﴾.
i.e. extremely sweet.
﴿وَهَـٰذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: al-ujāj is the bitter.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What is well known among the lexicographers is that al-ujāj is the intensely salty; and one says مَاءٌ مِلْحٌ (salt water), and one does not say مَالحٌ.
It is narrated from Ṭalḥa that he read ﴿وَهَذَا مَلِحٌ أُجَاجٌ﴾, with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the lām.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخاً وَحِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً﴾.
﴿بَرْزَخاً﴾ i.e. a barrier.
﴿وَحِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً﴾ i.e. a preventer.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ بَشَراً﴾.
By "the water" He means the sperm-drop, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ نَسَباً وَصِهْراً﴾.
It was said: it is the water from which the origins of living creatures were created.
And it was said: al-nasab (lineage) is the sons, who trace their lineage to him, and He created for him daughters, through whom come the in-laws (al-aṣhār).
Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: al-nasab is the (kinship) that is not ṣihr, from His saying, the Exalted, ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهَاتُكُمْ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَأَنْ تَجْمَعُوا بَيْنَ الأُخْتَيِنِ إلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾.
And al-ṣihr is the one whom it is lawful for him to marry.
ʿUmayra, the client of Ibn ʿAbbās, narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him — and it is the statement of al-Ḍaḥḥāk — that he said: "Seven are forbidden through lineage, and seven through marriage (ṣihr)." Then he recited ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهَاتُكُمْ وَبَنَاتُكُمْ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَأَنْ تَجْمَعُوا بَيْنَ الأُخْتَيْنِ إلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾.
And it was said: of al-ṣihr there are five: ﴿وَأُمَّهَاتُكُم اللاَّتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ.. إلى وَحَلاَئِلُ أَبْنَائِكُمْ﴾. This is the wording of al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
There is disagreement about the difference between «الخَتَن» and «الصِّهْرِ».
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: al-akhtān are everyone on the side of the wife,
such as the wife's father, her brother and her paternal uncle.
And al-aṣhār includes all of this; one says: صاهرَ فلانٌ إلى بني فلان and أصهَرَ إليهم (so-and-so married into the tribe of so-and-so).
Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: al-akhtān are the wife's father, her brother and her paternal uncle.
And al-ṣihr is the husband of a man's daughter, and his brother, his father and his paternal uncle.
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said — in the narration of Abū Sulaymān al-Jawzajānī —: a man's akhtān are the husbands of his daughters, his sisters, his paternal aunts, his maternal aunts and of every unmarriageable (maḥram) relative of his.
And his aṣhār are every unmarriageable blood relative of his wife.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What is most fitting here is that the statement on al-aṣhār be what al-Aṣmaʿī said, and that it be from the side of both of them together, because one says: صَهَرْتُ الشَّيْءَ, i.e. I mixed the thing, so each of the two has mixed with the other.
And the most fitting regarding al-akhtān is what Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said, for two reasons:
The first: the ḥadīth traced back to the Prophet (marfūʿ). Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated from Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qusayṭ, from Muḥammad ibn Usāma ibn Zayd, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for you, O ʿAlī, you are my khatan (son-in-law) and the father of my children; you are from me and I am from you." This indicates that the daughter's husband is a khatan.
The other reason is that one says: خَتَنَه, when he cut it; so the husband has been cut off from his own family and has cut the woman off from her family, and thus he is more deserving of this name.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَانَ ٱلْكَافِرُ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِ ظَهِيراً﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. a helper.
Al-Ḥasan said: i.e. an aid to Satan against Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in acts of disobedience.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلاَّ مُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً﴾.
Qatāda said: i.e. a bearer of good tidings of Paradise, and a warner against the Fire.

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿قُلْ مَآ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ أَن يَتَّخِذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلاً﴾.
Qatāda said: through obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ فَسْئَلْ بِهِ خَبِيراً﴾.
Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: i.e. ask about Him. A number of the lexicographers have related this, that "the bāʾ" has the meaning of "عَنْ" (about), as He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿سَأَلَ سَائِلٌ بِعَذَابٍ وَاقِعٍ﴾, and the poet said:
هَلاَّ سَأَلْتِ الخَيْلَ يا ابْنَةَ مَالِكٍ * إنْ كنتِ جَاهِلةًَ بما لم تَعْلَمي
(Why did you not ask the horsemen [about it], O daughter of Mālik, if you were ignorant of what you did not know?)
ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān (al-Akhfash the Younger) said: The people of reasoning reject that the bāʾ has the meaning of "عن", because this would corrupt the meanings. He said: Rather, this is like the Arabs' saying: لو لقيتَ فلاناً لَلَقِيكَ به الأسدُ ("had you met so-and-so, the lion would have met you through him"), i.e. by your meeting him, the lion would have met you.
And the meaning is: so ask, by your asking, according to what preceded.

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ بُرُوجاً﴾.
Qatāda said: i.e. stars.
Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated from Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: al-burūj are the great stars.
Ismāʿīl narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Rāfiʿ, who said: al-burūj are palaces in the sky.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Everything that is apparent and manifest is called burj; from this it is said: تبرَّجتِ المرأةُ (the woman displayed her adornment), and بَرَجَ بَرْجَاً, when it became apparent.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَاجاً وَقَمَراً مُّنِيراً﴾.
﴿سِرَاجَاً﴾ means the sun.
And it is read ﴿سُرُجاً﴾ (lamps).
And it was said: for whoever reads this reading, the meaning according to him is: and He placed lamps in the constellations (al-burūj).
If it is said: He has repeated the mention of the moon, while He has said ﴿سُرُجاً﴾ and the moon is included in them?
The answer is: the mention of the moon was repeated because of its superiority over them, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فِيهمَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ ٱللَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ خِلْفَةً﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. this one succeeds that one, and that one succeeds this one.
Al-Ḥasan said: Whoever forgot some of his remembrance and thanks during the day has an opportunity to make amends at night, and whoever forgot it at night has an opportunity to make amends during the day.
And it was said: ﴿خِلْفَةً﴾ means differing, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿واخْتِلاَفِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The most fitting of these statements is Mujāhid's.
The meaning is: each of them succeeds the other; it is derived from al-khilf, and from it is خَلَفَ فلانٌ فلاناً بخيرٍ أو شرٍّ (so-and-so succeeded so-and-so with good or evil), and from it is the saying of Zuhayr:
بها العِينُ والآرَامُ يَمْشِينَ خِلْفَةً * وأَطْلاؤُهَا يَنْهَضْنَ منْ كُلِّ مَجْثَم
(In it the wild cows and white gazelles walk one after another, and their young rise up from every resting-place.)

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَىٰ ٱلأَرْضِ هَوْناً﴾.
Everyone is His servant, but He attributed them to Himself because He chose them, as one says: the House of Allah, and the She-camel of Allah.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَىٰ ٱلأَرْضِ هَوْناً﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. with dignity and tranquillity.
Al-Ḥasan said: Learned and forbearing; if others behave ignorantly toward them, they do not behave ignorantly.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الجَاهِلُونَ قَالُواْ سَلاَماً﴾.
Mujāhid said: i.e. (words of) rightness.
Sībawayh said: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb claimed that like it is your saying to a man: "سلاماً", meaning "disassociation (tasallum) from you", just as you say: "براءةً منك" (quittance from you). He said: And he claimed that this verse — according to what he claimed — is Meccan.
And the Muslims at that time had not been commanded to greet the polytheists with salām; rather it is according to his saying "tasallum": there is neither good between us and you, nor evil.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ وَالَّذِينَ يِبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّداً وَقِيَاماً﴾.
One says: باتَ (he spent the night) when night overtook him, whether he slept or did not sleep, as the poet said:
فَبِتْنَا قِيَامَاً عندَ رَأْسِ جَوَادِنا * يُزَاولُنَا عَنْ نفسِهِ ونُزَاوِلُهُ
(We spent the night standing at the head of our steed; it struggles with us to free itself, and we struggle with it.)

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَاماً﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: i.e. destruction, and he recited:
وَيَوْمُ النِّسِارِ، وَيَوْمُ الجِفَارِ * كَانَا عَذَاباً، وكَانَا غَرَامَاً
(The day of al-Nisār and the day of al-Jifār were a torment, and were a ruin [gharām].)
Al-Farrāʾ said: ﴿كَانَ غَرَاماً﴾ i.e. pressing and clinging; and from it: فلانٌ غريمي (so-and-so is my creditor), i.e. he presses in demanding.
And al-gharām according to most lexicographers is the severest torment.
Al-Aʿshā said:
إنْ يعاقِبْ يكُنْ غَرَامَاً * وإنْ يُعْطِ جَزِيلاً فإنَّه لا يُبَالي
(If he punishes, it is a lasting torment; and if he gives abundantly, he does not care [how much].)
Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: Allah demanded of them the price of the blessings, and when they did not bring it, He made them pay its price (gharramahum) and admitted them into the Fire.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَنفَقُواْ لَمْ يُسْرِفُواْ وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُواْ﴾.
Sufyān said: ﴿لَمْ يُسْرِفُواْ﴾: they did not spend in what is not rightful.
﴿وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُواْ﴾: they did not withhold from what is rightful.
The best of what has been said is what Abū ʿAlī "al-Ḥasan ibn Ghulayb" narrated to us; he said: ʿImrān ibn Abī ʿImrān narrated to me; he said: Khallād ibn Sulaymān al-Ḥaḍramī narrated to us; he said: ʿAmr ibn Labīd narrated to me, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥulabī, about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَنفَقُواْ لَمْ يُسْرِفُواْ وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُواْ وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَاماً﴾; he said:
- Whoever spends in other than obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that is extravagance (al-isrāf).
- And whoever withholds from obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that is stinginess (al-iqtār).
- And whoever spends in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that is the right measure (al-qawām).
﴿وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَاماً﴾ i.e. just (a middle way).
Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā (Thaʿlab) said: One says: هذا قِوَامُ الأمرِ ومِلاَكُه (this is the mainstay of the matter and its support).
Some of the lexicographers said: This is a mistake; one only says: هذا قَوَامُ الأمر, and he adduced His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَاماً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What is correct is what Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said, and the two meanings are different: qawām with fatḥa is uprightness and justice, as Labīd said:
وَاحْبُ المُجَامِلَ بالجزَيلِ، وَصَرْمُهُ * باقٍ إذا ضَلَعَتْ وَزَاغَ قَوَامُهَا
(Give generously to the one who treats you kindly; yet breaking off with him remains [possible] when [the friendship] becomes crooked and its uprightness deviates.)
And qiwām with kasra is that on which the matter lasts and is established.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَدْعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَـٰهًا آخَرَ﴾.
Abū Wāʾil said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Which sin is the greatest? He said: That you associate a partner with Allah, Exalted and Majestic, when He created you.
I said: Then which? He said: That you kill your child for fear that it will eat with you, and that you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." Then ʿAbd Allāh recited ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَدْعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَـٰهًا آخَرَ﴾, the verse.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذٰلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَاماً﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is a valley in Hell.
Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī said: One says: لقيَ أَثَامَ ذلك, i.e. the recompense of that.
Al-Qutabī (Ibn Qutayba) said: al-athām is the recompense of punishment, and he recited:
* "وَالعُقُوقُ لَهُ أَثَامُ" *
(and undutifulness [to parents] has its recompense)
Abū Jaʿfar said: The soundest of what has been said on this — and it is the statement of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh — is that the meaning is: he will meet the recompense of sin (al-athām), as He, Glorified is He, said ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَة﴾ [Translator's note: i.e. with an omitted muḍāf, "the people of the town"].
And He explained the recompense of sin, saying ﴿يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ العَذَابُ يَوْمَ القِيَامةِ﴾, just as the poet explained in his saying:
متى تَأْتِنا تُلْمِمْ بِنَا في دِيَارِنَا * تَجِدْ حَطَباً جَزْلاً وَنَاراً تأجَّجا
(Whenever you come to us, alighting with us in our homes, you will find thick firewood and a blazing fire.)
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَدْعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَـٰهًا آخَرَ﴾ to the end of the verse, the polytheists said: He has claimed that there is no repentance for us. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿إلاَّ مَنْ تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعمِلَ عَمَلاً صَالِحاً﴾, i.e. repented from polytheism and entered Islam.
This was revealed in Mecca, and Allah revealed ﴿قُلْ يَا عِبَاديَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللهِ إن الله يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعَاً﴾, the verse. Then, in Medina, eight years later, He revealed ﴿وَمَنْ يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِنَاً مُتَعَمِّدَاً فَجَزَاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ﴾, and it is unqualified (mubham), with no way out of it.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ حَسَنَاتٍ﴾.
ʿĀṣim narrated from Abū ʿUthmān, from Salmān, who said: "The believer reads at the beginning of his record the evil deeds, and sees the good deeds below that. Then he looks at its face, and looks at its top, and behold, it is all good deeds, so he says ﴿هَاؤُمُ اقْرَءُوا كِتَابِيَهْ﴾. Those are the ones whose evil deeds Allah replaces with good deeds."
Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: i.e. He gives them faith in exchange for polytheism.
Al-Ḥasan said: Some people say the replacement is in the Hereafter, on the Day of Resurrection, but it is not so; the replacement is only in this world: Allah gives them in exchange faith for polytheism, sincerity for doubt, and chastity for wickedness.
Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: A good deed is not put in place of the evil deed; rather, repentance is put in place of the evil deed, and the good deed along with the repentance.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن تَابَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحاً فَإِنَّهُ يَتُوبُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَتاباً﴾.
i.e. an emphasised repentance; i.e. when he does good works after the repentance, it is said: تَابَ مَتَاباً, i.e. a pleasing, accepted repentance.

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya said: It means singing.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It means polytheism.
The origin of al-zūr in the language is lying, and polytheism is the gravest lie.
His saying ﴿وَإِذَا مَرُّواْ بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِراماً﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "باللَّغو" means by polytheism.
It is also narrated from him: when they mention sexual relations, they speak of it by allusion.
Al-Ḥasan said: al-laghw is all acts of disobedience.
The origin of al-laghw in the language is: that which ought to be cancelled (yulghā), i.e. discarded.
i.e. they left it, and held themselves too noble for it.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَمْ يَخِرُّواْ عَلَيْهَا صُمّاً وَعُمْيَاناً﴾.
i.e. they did not feign heedlessness of them and leave them, so as to be in the position of one who neither hears nor sees.

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: i.e. obedient to You.
Then He said ﴿وَٱجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَاماً﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: i.e. make us leaders (imams) who are followed in good.
Al-Ḥasan said: i.e. make us follow the God-fearing who were before us, and let those after us follow us.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ مَا يَعْبَأُ بِكُمْ رَبِّي لَوْلاَ دُعَآؤُكُمْ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: i.e. what would my Lord do with you, were it not for His calling you to worship Him and obey Him?!
This is the best of what has been said about the verse, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿مَا يَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ بِعَذَابِكُمْ إنْ شَكَرْتُمْ وَآمَنْتُمْ﴾.
The origin of ﴿يَعْبَأُ﴾ is from al-ʿibʾ, which is weight (burden); and the poet's saying:
كأنَّ بصَدْرِهِ وبجانِبْيهِ * عَبِيَراً بَاتَ يَعْبأُهُ عَرُوسُ
(As if on his chest and his two sides were perfume that a bridegroom had spent the night piling on.)
i.e. he puts some of it on top of other.
i.e. what weight do you have with your Lord, were it not that He wanted to call you to His obedience!?
Al-Qutabī said: The meaning is: my Lord would not care about punishing you, were it not for your calling on others besides Him, i.e. were it not for your polytheism.
Then He, Glorified is He, said ﴿فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزَاماً﴾.
Masrūq narrated from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: It means the day of Badr.
Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said likewise.
Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: i.e. the denial will be binding, clinging to you, and you will not be granted repentance.
Al-Qutabī said: i.e. the punishment will be binding (lizām).
Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿لِزَاماً﴾ i.e. decisive (a separation).
Muslim ibn ʿAmmār said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās reading it ﴿فقد كذَّب الكافرون فسوفَ يكونُ لِزَاماً﴾.
Abū Zayd said: I heard Qaʿnab reading ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزَاماً﴾ with fatḥa on the lām [i.e. lazāman].
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "لَزِم", and the first is the maṣdar of "لُوزِمَ".
Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us; he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us; he said: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿قُلْ مَا يَعْبَأُ بِكُمْ رَبِّي لَوْلاَ دُعَآؤُكُمْ﴾ — he says: were it not for your faith.
And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed the disbelievers that He has no need of them if He did not create them believers; and had He any need of them, He would have made faith beloved to them, as He made it beloved to the believers. ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزَاماً﴾ — he said: he says: death.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِي نَزَّلَ ٱلْفُرْقَانَ عَلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ﴾.
And ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr read ﴿عَلى عِبَادِهِ﴾.
﴿تَبَارَكَ﴾ is of the pattern تَفَاعَلَ from البَرَكة, which is the alighting of good.
And from it: "so-and-so is مُبَارَك", that is, good alights wherever he alights; it is derived from البَرْك and البَرَكة, both of which are the maṣdar (verbal noun).
And ﴿الفُرْقَانَ﴾ is the Qurʾān, because it distinguishes (فَرَقَ) between truth and falsehood, and between the believer and the disbeliever.
And "النَّذير" is the one who warns of the punishment of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He; and everyone who warns is نذير and مُنذِر.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِيۤ إِن شَآءَ جَعَلَ لَكَ خَيْراً مِّن ذٰلِكَ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ﴾.
Sufyān related from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit from Khaythama that he said:
It was said to the Prophet ﷺ: "If you wish, We will give you the treasures of this world and its keys — such as was not given to anyone before you and will not be given to anyone after you — and that will not diminish anything of yours in the Hereafter.
And if you wish, We will gather that for you in the Hereafter." He said: "Let it be gathered for me in the Hereafter."
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِيۤ إِن شَآءَ جَعَلَ لَكَ خَيْراً مِّن ذٰلِكَ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ وَيَجْعَل لَّكَ قُصُوراً﴾.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ إِذَا رَأَتْهُمْ مِّن مَّكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ سَمِعُواْ لَهَا تَغَيُّظاً وَزَفِيراً﴾.
Two views have been stated on the meaning of this:
The first: they heard, from those being punished in it, raging and roaring.
The proponent of this view cited as evidence His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهُمْ فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ وشَهِيقٌ﴾.
The other view: that the meaning is: they heard it raging against them, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿تَكَادُ تَمَيَّزُ مِنَ الغَيْظِ﴾.
The second view is more fitting, because He said ﴿سَمِعُواْ لَهَا﴾ and did not say "they heard in it" or "from it".
The implied construction (taqdīr) is: they heard from it a sound of raging.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿دَعَوْاْ هُنَالِكَ ثُبُوراً﴾.
Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, destruction.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says: "ما ثَبَرَك عن كذا?", that is, what turned you away from it?
So المثبور is the one turned away from good.
And the meaning is: they say "وا ثُبُوراه" (O my destruction!).
And ʿAlī ibn Zayd related from Anas ibn Mālik from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The first to be clothed in a garment from Hell is Iblīs: he puts it on [his forehead] and drags it, saying 'O my destruction!', and his offspring follow him, saying 'O our destruction!'; and it is said to them: Do not call today for one destruction, but call for many destructions."

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أَذٰلِكَ خَيْرٌ أَمْ جَنَّةُ ٱلْخُلْدِ ٱلَّتِي وُعِدَ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾.
There is no good in that; it is only [spoken] according to your deeds and to what you do.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ وَعْداً مَّسْئُولاً﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: That is, He is asked for it; and that is the saying of the angels, may Allah bless them: ﴿رَبَّنَا وَأَدْخِلْهُمْ جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ الَّتِي وَعَدْتَهُمْ﴾.
And it was said: What is meant by that is their saying: ﴿لَوْلاَ أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ فَيَكُونَ مَعَهُ نَذِيَراً. أو يُلْقَى إلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ أَوْ تَكُونُ لَهُ جنَّةٌ يَأْكُلُ مِنْهَا﴾?

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The Messiah, ʿUzayr and the angels.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ نَسُواْ ٱلذِّكْرَ وَكَانُواْ قَوْماً بُوراً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, perishing.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Whatever perishes, is ruined or is left unsold is called بائر; and from it: "بارتِ السوق" (the market stagnated) and "بارت الأيِّم" (the unmarried woman found no husband). And "بُور" applies to the singular and the plural, according to the view of most grammarians.
And some of them said: the singular is بائر and the plural بُور, just as one says عَائِد and عُوْذ, and هَائِد and هُوْد.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوكُمْ بِمَا تَقُولُونَ﴾.
That is, in your saying that they are gods.
And al-Farrāʾ reported that it is also read ﴿فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوكُمْ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning on this reading is: they have belied you by their saying ﴿مَا كَان يَنْبغِي لَنَا أنْ نتَّخِذَ مِنْ دُوْنِكَ مِنْ أَوْلياءَ﴾.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَمَا تَسْتَطِيعُونَ صَرْفاً وَلاَ نَصْراً﴾.
Yūnus said: الصَّرْف is الحلية «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably الحيلة, "stratagem", which fits what follows.]», from their saying "so-and-so manages (يتصرَّف) things"; that is, they are not able to turn the punishment away from themselves, nor to help themselves.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يَظْلِم مِّنكُمْ نُذِقْهُ عَذَاباً كَبِيراً﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: [The wrongdoing is] associating partners with Allah.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيراً﴾.
That is, He determined for each thing what sets it right and what sustains it.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَمْلِكُونَ مَوْتاً وَلاَ حَيَـاةً وَلاَ نُشُوراً﴾.
One says: أَنْشَر اللهُ المَوْتى، فَنَشَروا (Allah raised the dead, and they rose).

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ إِنْ هَـٰذَا إِلاَّ إِفْكٌ ٱفْتَرَاهُ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: ﴿إِفْكٌ﴾ means a lie.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَأَعَانَهُ عَلَيْهِ قَوْمٌ آخَرُونَ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid that he said: The Jews.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَقَدْ جَآءُوا ظُلْماً وَزُوراً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, a lie.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied construction (taqdīr) is: they have come with (بـ) wrong and falsehood.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالُوۤاْ أَسَاطِيرُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ ٱكْتَتَبَهَا فَهِيَ تُمْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, the tales of the ancients.
Qatāda said: ﴿وَأَصِيلاً﴾ means: in the evening.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالُواْ مَالِ هَـٰذَا ٱلرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ ٱلطَّعَامَ وَيَمْشِي فِي ٱلأَسْوَاقِ﴾.
That is: what is the matter with him, eating and walking?
Then they demanded that an angel be with him as a partner: ﴿لَوْلاۤ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ﴾? Yet He, Mighty and Majestic is He, has said ﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ مَلَكَاً لَجَعَلْنَاهُ رَجُلاً وَلَلَبَسْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ مَا يَلْبِسُوْنَ﴾,
that is: had We sent down an angel, they would not have understood from him until he became a man; and if he were a man, they would still not believe except with [some] interpretation.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا بَعْضَكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ فِتْنَةً أَتَصْبِرُونَ وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ بَصِيراً﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿فتنةً﴾ means a trial.
Abū Jaʿfar said: الفتنة in the language is testing.
The meaning is: We made the noble a trial for the lowly, and the lowly a trial for the noble.
It is related that a noble man would want to embrace Islam, and what prevented him from that was that someone beneath him had embraced Islam before him, so he would say: "I will be reproached for his having preceded me."
And some of the disabled and the poor would say: "Why was I not rich and healthy, so that I might embrace Islam?"
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَتَصْبِرُونَ﴾? That is: if you are patient, you already know the reward of the patient.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
Then He reported that those who do not believe in the Hereafter demand signs such as were given to no one, and said, Mighty and Majestic is He:
﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَرْجُونَ لِقَآءَنَا لَوْلاَ أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ أَوْ نَرَىٰ رَبَّنَا لَقَدِ ٱسْتَكْبَرُواْ فِيۤ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَعَتَوْا عُتُوّاً كَبِيراً﴾.
And العُتُوّ is overstepping bounds in what is improper.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةَ لاَ بُشْرَىٰ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً﴾.
ʿAṭiyya related from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: ﴿حِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً﴾: he said: utterly forbidden.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, the angels say to them: "It is utterly forbidden to you that you should have good tidings today" — meaning the disbelievers.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning is: good tidings are forbidden to you; and from this comes the judge's حَجْر (interdiction), which is simply his restraining [someone], and from this comes the حَجْر of a person.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَدِمْنَآ إِلَىٰ مَا عَمِلُواْ مِنْ عَمَلٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿وَقَدِمْنَا﴾ means: We turned to (عَمَدْنا).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The origin of this is that one who comes to a place makes for it and heads towards it.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُ هَبَآءً مَّنثُوراً﴾.
Abū Isḥāq related from al-Ḥārith from ʿAlī that he said: الهَبَاء المنثور is the sunbeam [that enters through the window-opening.
Abū Jaʿfar said: هباء is the plural of هباءة, and it is said of what appears in the sunbeam].
It resembles dust: هَبَاء منثور (scattered motes); and what flies up from under the horses' hooves is called هباء مُنبثّ.
Its origin is from أَهْبَأَ التُّرابَ إهباءً when he stirs up the dust, as was said:
* "مَنِيناً كأنَّه أَهْبَاءُ" *
(Fine and weak, as if it were dust-motes.)

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ أَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرّاً وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلاً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What is said about this is like what is said about His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ أَمْ جَنَّةُ الخُلْدِ﴾?
And al-Farrāʾ holds that there is no question in this at all.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلاً﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, a refuge and an abode.
Abū Jaʿfar said: المَقِيل in the language is the place of staying at the time of the midday rest (القيلولة) specifically; the people of Paradise go back to their wives for about the length of half a day, so the people of Paradise take their midday rest in Paradise, and the people of the Fire in the Fire, at that time.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنُزِّلَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ تَنزِيلاً﴾.
Qatāda said: The angels of each heaven, one heaven after another, will descend, and the creatures will say to them: "Is our Lord, Mighty and Majestic is He, among you?" — and he mentioned the ḥadīth.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْحَقُّ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ﴾.
Because the dominion of this world is passing.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ ٱلظَّالِمُ عَلَىٰ يَدَيْهِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: "ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ" was a close friend of Umayya ibn Khalaf. Word reached Umayya that ʿUqba had [resolved] to embrace Islam, so he came to him and said to him: "My face is forbidden to your face if you do not disbelieve in Muḥammad ﷺ." So the wretch did it, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظَّالِمُ عَلَى يَدَيْهِ يَقُولُ يَا لَيْتَنِي اتَّخَذْتُ مَعَ الرَّسُولِ سَبِيلاً. يَا وَيْلَتَى لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أَتَّخِذْ فُلانَاً خَلِيلاً﴾.
And Abū Rajāʾ said: "فلان" (so-and-so) is Satan; and an argument was made for the proponent of this view that after it comes ﴿وَكَانَ الشَّيْطَانُ لِلإنْسَانِ خَذُولاً﴾.
The first view is the one the exegetes hold.
ʿUthmān al-Jazarī related from Miqsam from Ibn ʿAbbās that this came down concerning "ʿUqba" and "Umayya".
And in Miqsam's narration: As for "ʿUqba", he was among the captives on the day of Badr, and the Prophet ﷺ ordered that he be killed. He said: "Am I to be killed rather than them?" He said: "Yes, for your disbelief and your insolence." He said: "Who will there be for the children?" He said: "The Fire." Then ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib stood up and killed him.
As for "Umayya ibn Khalaf", the Prophet ﷺ killed him with his own hand; he had said: "By Allah, I will surely kill Muḥammad"; that reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "I will kill him, if Allah wills."
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ said, from Mujāhid: "Umayya" said to ʿUqba: "Have you turned Sabian (i.e. changed your religion)?" ʿUqba said: "I only made some food, and Muḥammad refused to eat of it until I testified to his messengership."
What "Abū Rajāʾ" said does not contradict this, because this happened through Satan's leading astray and his making things seem attractive, so it may be attributed to him on this basis.

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلرَّسُولُ يٰرَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِي ٱتَّخَذُواْ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ مَهْجُوراً﴾.
Mujāhid and Ibrāhīm said: That is, they said about it what is not true.
Ibrāhīm said: Have you not seen how the sick man يَهْجُر? That is, he raves.
And it was said: ﴿مَهْجُوراً﴾ means abandoned.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوّاً مِّنَ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: ﴿عَدُوَّاً﴾ may be in the sense of "enemies" (plural), and it may be for one.
And in some narrations from Ibn ʿAbbās, what is meant by it is "Abū Jahl" «[Translator's note: the source prints "أو جهل"; presumably أبو جهل.]».

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً وَاحِدَةً كَذَلِكَ﴾.
It was said: This is the complete stop (al-tamām).
And the meaning is: We sent it down in parts, to make your heart firm by it — thus [is] the making firm, as He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ أَنْ ثَبَّتْنَاكَ لَقَدْ كِدْتَ تَرْكَنُ إلَيهِمْ شَيْئَاً قَلِيَلاً﴾.
Because when He sent it down in parts, there was in it the answer to what they asked at its time, and in that was a making firm; so it was said: the complete stop is at His saying ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾.
[And it was said: the complete stop is at His saying "جملةً واحدة".]
And the meaning is: those who disbelieve said: "Why was the Qurʾān not sent down to him all at once, like the Torah and the Gospel?" — and the meaning of this is: why was it sent down in parts? So He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِ فُؤَادَكَ﴾, that is, We sent it down in parts to make your heart firm by it.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَرَتَّلْنَاهُ تَرْتِيلاً﴾.
Mughīra related from Ibrāhīm that he said: It was sent down in parts.
And al-Ḥasan said: Whenever the Prophet ﷺ was asked about something, its answer came down, until its revelation was completed in about twenty years.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَأْتُونَكَ بِمَثَلٍ إِلاَّ جِئْنَاكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَأَحْسَنَ تَفْسِيراً﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, in detail.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There is an omission in the statement.
The meaning is: and better in explanation than their example; and such a thing is often omitted.

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ شَرٌّ مَّكَاناً﴾.
In the noble ḥadīth: (People will be gathered in three classes: riding, walking, and on their faces. Anas said: It was said: O Messenger of Allah, how will they be gathered on their faces? He said: The One who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces.)

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مَعَهُ أَخَاهُ هَارُونَ وَزِيراً﴾.
Saʿīd related from Qatāda that he said: That is, a helper and a support.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَّمَّا كَذَّبُواْ ٱلرُّسُلَ أَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ﴾.
It was said: Does this require that the people of Noah denied others besides Noah ﷺ?
And it was answered: Whoever denies one prophet has denied all the prophets, because the prophets all believe in Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and in all His Books.
And it was said: This is as one says "so-and-so rides riding-animals (الدوابّ)" even if he rides only one, that is, he rides this kind.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَاداً وَثَمُودَاْ وَأَصْحَابَ ٱلرَّسِّ﴾.
Qatāda said: They were people of a stream (فَلْج) in al-Yamāma, and of wells.
Mujāhid said: "The people of al-Rass" lived by a well of theirs whose name was al-Rass, and they were named after it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: الرسّ according to the lexicographers is any well not lined with stone; and from it is the poet's saying:
* "تَنَابِلةٍ يَحْفِرونَ الرَّسَاسَا" *
(Short, sluggish men who dig the wells.)
He means the wells of the mines.
And it is related that they killed their prophet and رسّوه in a well, that is, they thrust him into it.
However, Qatāda said: The people of the Thicket and the people of al-Rass are two nations to both of whom "Shuʿayb" ﷺ was sent, and they were punished with two punishments.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُرُوناً بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ كَثِيراً﴾.
Qatāda said: It has reached us that a qarn (generation) is seventy years.
And the meaning of ﴿تَبَّرْنَا﴾ is: We destroyed and annihilated.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَتَوْا عَلَى ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلَّتِيۤ أُمْطِرَتْ مَطَرَ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾.
Qatāda said: He means the city of the people of Lot.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ كَانُواْ لاَ يَرْجُونَ نُشُوراً﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, a reckoning and a resurrection.
It was said: ﴿يَرْجُونَ﴾ here means: they fear.
And whoever denies the existence of words with opposite meanings (al-aḍdād) said: ﴿يَرْجُونَ﴾ is in its usual sense, that is, they do not hope for the reward of the Hereafter, and so guard against sins.
